findings.explanation: The Universal Forwarder is downloaded from splunk.com and is not a Splunkbase app; splunkbase.splunk.com/app/617 returns 404 and ID 617 is absent from data/splunkbase-catalog.json. The false ID is repeated in dataSources and detailedImplementation. SC4SNMP is Splunkbase 6266 and SNMP Modular Input is 1537 per the catalog.
findings.quote: APC PowerNet-MIB / AirIR-MIB field extractions — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
findings.suggested_fix: Remove "Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)" and cite Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase 6266) or SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase 1537).

findings.explanation: No OID is named for power factor. In PowerNet-MIB the output power factor is upsPhaseOutputPowerFactor (.1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.1.9.3.3.1.19, in hundredths) in the per-phase output table, mainly on three-phase and modular UPS models; many single-phase Smart-UPS units may not expose it. The reader cannot tell what to poll or whether their model supports it.
findings.quote: `sourcetype="snmp:apc:ups"` (APC PowerNet / AirIR / ATS / NetBotz OIDs per deployment)
findings.suggested_fix: Name upsPhaseOutputPowerFactor (hundredths, indexed by output and phase) as the source, note that it is per phase and that the SPL averages across phases per `ups_name`, and tell the reader to confirm their model returns it (snmpwalk the upsPhaseOutputPhaseTable) before deploying.

findings.explanation: "-7d" is the search time range, not a threshold. The SPL has no threshold at all: it draws a 7-day, 1-hour-span average power factor line per UPS.
findings.suggested_fix: Say: charts the hourly average output power factor (0-1) of each APC UPS over the last 7 days, so facilities can spot a drift below about 0.9. Point out that it is a trend report, not an alert.

findings.explanation: The SPL is a 7-day `timechart` trend with no alert condition; scheduling it over 24 h with throttling and paging contradicts both the SPL and the 'Line chart PF; SLA band 0.9–1.0' visualization. The rest is generic boilerplate (vendor API rate limits, HTTP 401/429) unrelated to SNMP polling.
findings.quote: Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. ... Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel
findings.suggested_fix: Describe dashboard use: poll the PF OID every 5 minutes, place the timechart on a facilities dashboard with a 0.9 reference line, and optionally add a separate alert if the 24 h average stays below the site's target. Validate against the PF shown on the UPS NMC web UI.

findings.explanation: No scenario names a real cause of a misleading power-factor reading, and "configured threshold" does not exist in the SPL.
findings.quote: Scheduled automation elevates `pf` without crossing configured threshold for UC-15.4.12.
findings.suggested_fix: Name real causes: very light UPS load (PF readings drop and become noisy at low load), UPS in bypass or eco mode, phases with no load reporting 0 and dragging the per-UPS average down, and firmware that reports PF as 0 when unavailable (filter `pf>0`).

findings.explanation: The SPL's OID name does not exist in PowerNet-MIB, the Splunkbase ID is false and the prose is template residue; this was not meaningfully SME-verified.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until an SME confirms the PF OID and scaling on a real APC UPS.

findings.explanation: The Schneider link is a PDU product category, not UPS documentation; the SC4SNMP link is a Splunkbase search URL.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the PowerNet-MIB reference / APC NMC documentation and https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/6266.

findings.explanation: It does not mention how efficiently the backup power units deliver electricity, which is what this chart shows.
findings.quote: We watch the physical data center for power, cooling, environment, and physical access.
findings.suggested_fix: e.g. "We draw a weekly chart of how efficiently each backup power unit is passing electricity to the servers, so we notice if it slowly gets worse."

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `upsAdvOutputPowerFactor` is not an object in PowerNet-MIB (the output PF object is upsPhaseOutputPowerFactor, .1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.1.9.3.3.1.19, hundredths, per phase; see https://circitor.fr/Mibs/Html/PowerNet-MIB.php). As written, the coalesce falls through to `output_power_factor`, which nothing in the UC defines, so the chart may be empty. Replace with the real field and filter `pf>0`.
`Cost` is a stretch: UPS output power factor reflects the IT load's characteristics, not utility billing power factor at the service entrance.

summary: A simple hourly power-factor trend chart per UPS, but the UC never names the real APC OID: the SPL's `upsAdvOutputPowerFactor` is not in PowerNet-MIB, and output power factor is a per-phase object. The collection text also cites a non-existent Splunkbase ID, and the surrounding prose treats a trend report as an alerting detection.
